hook.text: Robusta was always considered inferior—cheap filler for instant coffee. That reputation is changing fast.

buildup.text: Climate change threatens Arabica. Robusta is hardier, more disease-resistant, and grows at lower altitudes.

discovery.text: Fine Robusta initiatives now score and grade Robusta like Arabica. Some samples score above 80 points.

twist.text: Vietnam and Uganda are investing in specialty Robusta processing. The flavor gap with Arabica is narrowing rapidly.

climax.text: As Arabica supply shrinks, Robusta may become the dominant species. The industry's hierarchy is being rewritten.

punchline.text: Once dismissed, now essential. Robusta's time is arriving.

quiz.question: Why is Robusta becoming more important?
options: Climate change threatens Arabica, and Robusta quality is improving

details.summary: Long dismissed as cheap filler, robusta coffee is earning respect as farmers improve quality through better processing and careful cultivation. Fine robusta now competes in specialty markets. Vietnam has invested heavily in upgrading its robusta sector, changing global perceptions.
details.whyItMatters: Robusta's rehabilitation could reshape the coffee industry by expanding what counts as quality coffee and improving incomes for robusta-growing countries.
takeaways: Fine robusta is an emerging specialty category
Vietnam leads investment in robusta quality improvement
Better processing is closing the quality gap with arabica

faq.question: What makes fine robusta different from commodity robusta?
faq.answer: Fine robusta uses careful cherry selection, controlled processing, and quality-focused farming practices. The result is a cleaner cup with chocolate and nutty notes instead of the harsh bitterness associated with commodity robusta. It is scored independently of arabica on its own scale.

faq.question: Will robusta ever match arabica in price?
faq.answer: Top fine robustas already command prices comparable to mid-range arabica. However, arabica's larger flavor complexity and established prestige mean premium arabica will likely remain the market leader. Robusta's opportunity is in the growing middle market.
